text.autoconfig.YungsRoads-fabric-1_21.o: The distance between adjacent pathfinding nodes, in blocks.
Lower values follow the terrain more closely, but are slower to generate.
How strongly pathfinding is pulled toward the destination. 1.0 always finds the cheapest road.
Higher values generate faster but give slightly less optimal roads.
Show the structure region and road node at your position on the F3 screen.
yungsroads.setting.node_step_distance.de: The distance between neighboring nodes, in blocks. Lower values follow the terrain more closely, but are slower to generate.
yungsroads.setting.heuristic_weight.desc: How strongly routing is pulled toward the destination, by weighting the distance left in each node's search priority. 1 always finds the cheapest road. Higher values generate faster but can give slightly costlier roads.
yungsroads.setting.jitter_amount.descrip: How far jitter may shift the road sideways, in blocks. Higher values make roads wavier.
yungsroads.setting.slope_weight.descript: The extra cost of steep terrain. Each step cost is multiplied by (1 + Slope Weight × (grade² - Free Grade²)), so grades up to Free Grade cost nothing extra. Higher values make roads avoid hills and mountains more.
yungsroads.setting.free_grade.descriptio: The steepest grade that costs nothing extra to route over. Higher values let roads run straight over gentle rises instead of weaving around them, but weaken the pull toward switchbacks on hillsides. A 1-block rise over one node step is a grade of 0.125 at the default Node Step Distance.
yungsroads.setting.straighten_routes.des: Whether each route is straightened after routing, by cutting out nodes the road can bypass in a straight line that costs no more, stays within Max Grade, and doesn't cross water. Turn off to see the route as routing found it.
yungsroads.setting.max_grade.description: The steepest grade a road may have. Routing never crosses steeper terrain, and where the ground between nodes is steeper, the road cuts or tunnels through it. 1 is a 45 degree slope.
yungsroads.setting.water_weight.descript: The extra cost of bridging water. Added to the multiplier in each bridge's cost. Higher values make roads detour further to avoid rivers and lakes, or to find a shorter crossing.
yungsroads.setting.max_bridge_length.des: The longest bridge a road may build, in blocks. Roads cross rivers and lakes only on straight bridges, so wider water must be routed around. 0 disables bridges. Oceans are never crossed.
yungsroads.setting.smoothing_radius.desc: How far along the road its height is averaged, in blocks. Higher values give gentler slopes, with more cutting and filling to level the ground. 0 follows the terrain.
yungsroads.setting.max_cut_depth.descrip: The deepest a road may cut into the ground above it to stay level, in blocks. Where the ground rises higher, the road rises too, unless that would be steeper than Max Grade, where it tunnels through instead.
yungsroads.setting.max_fill_depth.descri: The deepest gap under a road that's filled with ground, in blocks. Deeper gaps, such as ravines and cave openings, are crossed on a land bridge instead.
yungsroads.setting.max_land_bridge_lengt: The longest dip in the terrain that a road crosses on a land bridge, in blocks, if it's deeper than Max Fill Depth. Longer dips are followed instead. Ravines and caves made by carvers always get a land bridge, since routing can't see them.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_edge_roug: How ragged the edges of land bridges are. 0 gives straight edges. Higher values move each edge block up to a block in or out.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_decay.des: How much of each land bridge's deck is missing, for a ruined look. Blocks are likelier to be missing toward the edges, and the center line is always kept. 0 keeps the whole deck.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_sag.descr: How far each land bridge's deck sags between its ends, as a fraction of its length. The sag is limited so the deck is never steeper than Max Grade. 0 gives straight decks.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_railing_d: The shortest drop beside a land bridge that gets a railing along its edge, in blocks, from the deck down to the ground. Lower values put railings along more of each bridge.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_railing_c: The percent chance that each spot where a land bridge railing could go gets one. 100 lines every edge with a drop beside it, and 0 places no railings.
yungsroads.glossary.node.definition: A point on the grid that roads are routed through. Neighboring nodes are Node Step Distance blocks apart.
yungsroads.glossary.step.definition: A move from a node to one of its 16 neighbors: the 8 around it, including diagonals, and the 8 a chess knight's move away, which allow smoother headings.
yungsroads.glossary.step_cost.definition: How much routing charges for one step. Routing picks the route with the lowest total cost, so costly terrain is avoided when a cheaper detour exists. A flat step on land costs its run.
yungsroads.glossary.bridge.definition: A straight crossing over water, from a node on one bank to the first dry node on the other. Bridges can head the same ways as steps, and their length is measured between the two bank nodes, so the shortest possible bridge is twice Node Step Distance. Like steps, bridges can't be steeper than Max Grade. Their extra cost per block makes roads take the shortest crossing that's worth it over a detour.
yungsroads.glossary.run.definition: The horizontal length of a step or bridge in blocks: Node Step Distance for each lattice move, or 1.41 or 2.24 times that for diagonal or knight's moves.
yungsroads.glossary.grade.definition: How steep a step is: its change in height divided by its run (rise over run). 0 is flat, 0.5 climbs 1 block every 2 blocks, and 1 is a 45 degree slope. Roads over water are measured at sea level.
yungsroads.glossary.water.definition: Ground below sea level, such as rivers and lakes. Steps never enter it, so roads only cross it on straight bridges at sea level. Oceans are never crossed.
yungsroads.glossary.search_priority.defi: Nodes are explored in order of search priority, lowest first, until the destination is reached.
yungsroads.glossary.cost_so_far.definiti: The total step cost of the cheapest known route from the start to a node.
yungsroads.glossary.distance_left.defini: The straight-line distance from a node to the destination, in blocks. Weighted by Heuristic Weight: at 1, routing always finds the cheapest road. Higher weights rush toward the destination, which generates faster but can give slightly costlier roads.
yungsroads.glossary.jitter.definition: A noise-based sideways shift applied to each node after routing, so roads look less straight. It doesn't affect cost.
yungsroads.glossary.land_bridge.definiti: A crossing over a hole or dip in the ground, such as a ravine or cave opening, built from bridge blocks at the height of the road on either side. Routing plans one over each dip in the terrain deeper than Max Fill Depth and up to Max Land Bridge Length long. Holes made by carvers, which routing can't see, get one wherever the road would be more than Max Fill Depth above the ground. Each bridge extends a few blocks past its rims and spans every gap beneath its deck. Railings line its edges wherever the drop beside them is at least Land Bridge Railing Drop.
yungsroads.glossary.road_type.definition: A style of road, set by a file in a datapack: how it's routed, how it's shaped to the terrain, and what it's built from. Each road gets one road type, chosen by the biomes along it.
yungsroads.glossary.road_network.definit: A dimension's roads, set by a file in a datapack: the structures they connect, and the road types they can get. Dimensions without one have no roads.
yungsroads.glossary.variant.definition: One of several sets of settings in a road type. Roads of the type are split between its variants at random, in proportion to each variant's weight.
yungsroads.screen.title: Road Debug
yungsroads.screen.singleplayer_only: The road debug screen only works in singleplayer.
yungsroads.screen.road_type.tooltip:
The road type whose settings you're editing. Only the road types this dimension's roads can get are listed: those in its road network, and its default road type (%s). Each road's road type is chosen by the biomes along it. Hover a road on the map to see which road type it got and why.
Road type settings are saved to a datapack, unlike the global settings.
yungsroads.screen.no_network: This dimension has no road network, so it has no roads or road types to tune. The map says how to add one.
yungsroads.screen.global.note: Saved to the mod's config file, and used by every road type.
yungsroads.screen.global.place_roads.des: Place road blocks. Turn off to see routes on the overlay without changing terrain.
yungsroads.screen.view.world_overlay.des: Draw routes as lines in the world. Hidden parts are drawn faintly through terrain.
yungsroads.screen.view.previous_roads.de: Draw the roads replaced by the last change in red, on the map and overlay.
yungsroads.screen.view.nodes.description: Mark each pathfinding node, on the map and overlay.
yungsroads.screen.view.region_borders.de: Draw structure region borders on the map.
yungsroads.screen.view.f3_info.descripti: Show the structure region and road node at your position on the F3 screen.
yungsroads.screen.view.terrain.tooltip:
Terrain shown on the map, one pixel per pathfinding node.
Height: surface height, shaded.
Slope: grade relative to Max Grade.
Cost: routing's cost multiplier, log scale up to 50x.
Purple can't be crossed. Slope and Cost use the road type you're editing, including unapplied changes.
yungsroads.screen.apply.tooltip: Regenerate roads within %s blocks with these settings, then place them in loaded chunks. Only re-places roads if only Place roads changed.
yungsroads.screen.revert.tooltip: Restore the settings and roads from before the last change. Press again to redo it.
yungsroads.screen.reset.tooltip: Reset the road types to the settings this world loaded with, and the global settings to their defaults. Press Apply to use them.
yungsroads.screen.save.tooltip: Save the applied settings: the global settings to the mod's config file, and the changed road types to a datapack in this world, used from the next time it loads.
yungsroads.screen.copy_json.tooltip: Copy the road type you're editing to the clipboard as a datapack file, with any unapplied changes.
yungsroads.screen.invalid: Fix the values shown in red before applying (%s)
yungsroads.screen.copied: Copied road type %s to the clipboard
yungsroads.status.saved: Saved global settings to the config file, and road types %s to this world's datapack %s. They're used from the next time the world loads.
yungsroads.status.saved_no_types: Saved global settings to the config file. No road types were changed.
yungsroads.formula.routing.title: Routing formulas
yungsroads.formula.max_grade: Steps above grade %s are never taken
yungsroads.formula.max_bridge_length: Bridges are at most %s blocks long
yungsroads.formula.search_priority: Search priority = cost so far + %s × distance left
yungsroads.formula.shaping.title: Shaping rules
yungsroads.formula.global.title: Global formulas
yungsroads.formula.smoothing: Road height = ground averaged over %s blocks each way
yungsroads.formula.cut: Ground up to %s blocks above the road is cut away
yungsroads.formula.fill: Gaps up to %s blocks below the road are filled, and deeper holes get a land bridge
yungsroads.formula.land_bridge: Dips up to %s blocks long get a land bridge
yungsroads.formula.railing: Land bridge edges with drops of %s+ blocks get railings
yungsroads.map.bridge_only: Only crossed by straight bridges, up to %s blocks long
yungsroads.map.step_cost: Steepest step cost: run × (1 + %s × max(0, %s² - %s²)) = run × %s
yungsroads.map.node: Node cost so far: %s, weighted distance left: %s, search priority: %s
yungsroads.map.no_network.text:
This dimension has no road network, so it has no roads.
To give it roads, add this file to a datapack, then reload the world:
%s
See the help page (?) for how.
yungsroads.map.network.title: Road network for %s
yungsroads.map.network.reload: As loaded with the world. Edit the datapack files and reload the world to change it. See the help page (?).
yungsroads.help.title: Help
yungsroads.help.overview.title: About this screen
yungsroads.help.overview.text:
Tune how roads are generated, and see the result right away. Edit settings on the left, then press Apply to regenerate the roads near you with them. The map shows the roads, and the terrain as routing sees it.
Applying re-places roads in chunks that already generated, which can overwrite anything built near them. Use a test world.
yungsroads.help.road_types.title: Road types
yungsroads.help.road_types.text:
Every road has a road type, which sets how it's routed, how it's shaped to the terrain, and what it's built from. Road types are datapack files in data/<namespace>/yungsroads/road_type, so datapacks can add their own or override the ones the mod ships with.
Each road's road type is chosen by the biomes along it. The biome is sampled every 64 blocks along the straight line between the road's ends, and each sample votes for the road types of the dimension's road network whose selection matches its biome. The road type with the most votes wins.
Selection: the biomes a road type is chosen for, as a biome, a list of biomes, or a biome tag.
Priority: decides between road types whose biomes overlap. In a biome that several road types match, only those with the highest priority get its vote. A tie in votes also goes to the higher priority.
Default: the road network's default road type gets the vote of every sample that none of its road types match. The Overworld's is yungsroads:default.
Variants: a road type can have several variants, each with its own settings. Roads of the road type are split between them at random, in proportion to each variant's weight. A variant with weight 3 gets three times as many roads as one with weight 1.
Hover a road on the map to see its road type and the votes that chose it.
yungsroads.help.road_networks.title: Road networks
yungsroads.help.road_networks.text:
Each dimension's roads are set by its road network, a datapack file named after the dimension: data/<namespace>/yungsroads/road_network/<dimension>.json, such as data/minecraft/yungsroads/road_network/overworld.json. Dimensions without one have no roads. Hover the label in the map's bottom left corner to see this dimension's road network.
structures: the structures its roads connect, as a structure, a list of structures, or a structure tag.
road_types: the road types its roads can get, as a road type, a list of road types, or a road type tag. Only these are listed on this screen. The Overworld's are the tag #yungsroads:overworld, so a datapack can add a road type to the Overworld with the tag file data/yungsroads/tags/yungsroads/road_type/overworld.json, without replacing its road network.
default_road_type: the road type that gets the vote of every sample that none of its road types match.
Adding a road type: tune a road type here, then press Copy Road Type JSON. Paste it into a new file data/<namespace>/yungsroads/road_type/<name>.json in a datapack, and change its selection to the biomes it's for. Then add <namespace>:<name> to the road types of each road network that should use it, such as with the tag file {"values": ["<namespace>:<name>"]}. Road types and road networks only load with the world, not with /reload, so reload the world, then tune the new road type here.
yungsroads.help.routing.title: Routing
yungsroads.help.routing.text: Routing finds where each road goes. It searches a grid of nodes for the route with the lowest total step cost, so roads avoid steep ground and water when a cheaper detour exists. These settings belong to the road type you're editing.
yungsroads.help.shaping.title: Shaping
yungsroads.help.shaping.text: Shaping fits a routed road to the terrain: how its height is smoothed, where the ground is cut or filled, and where it crosses dips on land bridges or bores through hills in tunnels. These settings belong to the road type you're editing.
yungsroads.help.global.title: Global
yungsroads.help.global.text: Global settings apply to every road type, and are saved to the mod's config file rather than a road type. Like road type settings, they're applied with the Apply button. Changing only Place roads re-places roads without regenerating them.
yungsroads.help.view.title: View
yungsroads.help.view.text:
View options only change what's drawn on the map and in the world, and take effect right away. Nothing here changes the roads.
On the map, drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and right-click to teleport. Hover a road to see its road type, and the costs routing sees at any spot.
yungsroads.help.saving.title: Applying and saving
yungsroads.help.saving.text:
Apply: regenerates the roads within %s blocks of you with the settings on the left, then re-places them in loaded chunks. Roads further away keep their old shape until they're regenerated.
Revert: restores the settings and roads from before the last change. Press it again to redo the change.
Reset: resets the road types to the settings this world loaded with, and the global settings to their defaults. Press Apply to use them.
Save: saves the global settings to the mod's config file, and the road types you changed to a datapack in this world's datapacks folder, named yungsroads_tuned. The datapack is used from the next time the world loads. It includes a README describing every setting, and can be copied into other worlds or a modpack.
Copy Road Type JSON: copies the road type you're editing to the clipboard, as a file for a datapack.
yungsroads.help.glossary.title: Glossary
yungsroads.docs.title: Road types tuned with YUNG's Roads
yungsroads.docs.intro: This datapack holds road types changed on YUNG's Roads' road debug screen. Each file in data/<namespace>/yungsroads/road_type overrides the road type with the same id, or adds a new one. To use them in another world, copy this folder into that world's datapacks folder, or add it to a modpack.
yungsroads.docs.choosing.title: How road types are chosen
yungsroads.docs.format.title: File format
yungsroads.docs.format.text: A road type has an optional selection, and either one set of settings or a list of weighted variants:
yungsroads.docs.settings.title: Settings
yungsroads.docs.settings.text: Each setting that's left out takes its default value. Unknown setting names are errors, so a misspelled setting is reported in the log rather than ignored.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.title: Blocks
yungsroads.docs.blocks.surfaces: The road's blocks and width over each kind of ground. Each column of the road uses the first surface that matches the ground there.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.target_blocks: The ground blocks the surface is used on.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.path_blockstates: The blocks the road is made of.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.fill_blockstates: Optional. The blocks that build up the ground under a road raised above it. Without it, the ground's own block is copied.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.road_size_variati: How much the road's width varies along its length.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.bridge_blockstate: The blocks bridges over water and land bridges are built from.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.bridge_railing_bl: Optional. The railings along the edges of land bridges with a drop beside them. Fences, walls, panes, and bars connect to each other. Without it, land bridges have no railings.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.tunnel_lining_blo: Optional. The blocks lining the walls and ceilings of tunnels. Without it, tunnels are bare, with only unstable blocks and fluids in their walls made solid.
yungsroads.docs.global.title: Global settings
yungsroads.docs.global.text: Node Step Distance and Heuristic Weight apply to every road type, so they're in the mod's config file instead of a road type's file.
